newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo RTB Bor 1996 copper cathode output 104,500 T.
newsitem.headline: Yugo RTB Bor 1996 copper cathode output 104,500 T.

text.p: Yugoslavia's copper mining and smelting works Rudarsko-topionicarski basen Bor (RTB Bor) produced 104,500 tonnes of cathode copper in 1996, some 20,000 tonnes below plan, the Belgrade newspaper Borba said on Monday.
RTB Bor's 1995 cathode copper output was 78,000 tonnes.
Overall production in the holding company's 20 enterprises, which employ some 20,000 people, was raised by around 18-20 percent against 1995, Borba said.
No one at RTB Bor was immediately available for comment.
A fall in prices of copper on world markets and the remaining "outer wall" of sanctions against Yugoslavia, barring access to international funding, hurt the complex financially.

"Around 60 to 70 percent of the basin's income is from exports, and without speedier opening of Western European, United States and other markets, we cannot raise sales, and thus production," RTB Bor general manager Ninoslav Cvetanovic was quoted by the paper as saying.
The complex planned to increase overall output by another 20 percent in 1997 and to produce around 137,000 tonnes of cathode copper and 35,000 tonnes of copper products.
"Copper production could be even higher if we secure sufficient quantities of blister copper and other secondary raw materials from abroad," Cvetanovic said.
He said deals had already been concluded for imports of more than 200,000 tonnes of concentrate, but a significant improvement was not expected in the first half of the year.
"Increasing production and exports requires additional turnover capital and it is very expensive on the local market." -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
